get.description:
Report that the process is running and able to serve requests.

This probe performs no dependency checks, so a failing database never causes the
orchestrator to restart a healthy process. Readiness and version endpoints are added by
task P-05.

Report whether this process can serve traffic.

Unlike ``/health`` (liveness), this checks the dependencies the API cannot work without, so an
orchestrator can take the instance out of the load balancer without restarting it. It answers
``503`` when a dependency is down.

Args:
    session: Per-request database session.
    response: Response object, used to set the status code.

Returns:
    The state of each dependency.

Report the application name, version, environment and commit that is running.

Args:
    settings: Application settings.

Returns:
    The build identity of the process.

display_name.title: Display Name

CandidateProfileCreate.title: CandidateProfileCreate
CandidateProfileCreate.description:
Body of ``POST /candidates/me``.

Preferences and visibility are not part of creation: a new profile starts private and with
empty preferences, and the candidate opts in through their own endpoints.

CandidateProfileRead.title: CandidateProfileRead
CandidateProfileRead.description: The candidate's own profile. It never includes identity data (email, role, ids).

CandidateProfileUpdate.title: CandidateProfileUpdate
CandidateProfileUpdate.description:
Body of ``PATCH /candidates/me``: only the fields sent are changed.

``summary`` and ``city`` accept ``null`` to clear them; ``display_name`` and ``languages``
cannot be null (send ``[]`` to clear the languages).

ConsentPurpose.title: ConsentPurpose
ConsentPurpose.description:
What the candidate may allow sharing of (US-08, FR-019, decision D-09).

Every purpose is denied until the candidate grants it explicitly: there is no shared profile
by default. ``DISCOVERY`` is what lets a company find the pseudonymised profile at all; the
other two decide which fields that projection may include (built by task B-06).

ConsentRead.title: ConsentRead
ConsentRead.description: The state of one purpose. A purpose never decided is reported as not granted.

granted.title: Granted
granted.description: True to allow sharing for this purpose, false to withdraw it.

ConsentUpdate.title: ConsentUpdate
ConsentUpdate.description:
Body of ``PUT /candidates/me/consents/{purpose}``: the candidate's decision.

``granted`` is required and strict: there is no default, so a client can never grant or
revoke a purpose by accident. ``policy_version`` is optional; when it is omitted the server
records the version of the privacy text it currently publishes.

ConsentsRead.title: ConsentsRead
ConsentsRead.description: Every purpose, always present, so a client never has to guess a missing one.

ContractType.title: ContractType
ContractType.description: Kinds of engagement the candidate is open to.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest
LoginRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /auth/login``.

There is deliberately no ``role`` field: the role always comes from the stored account.

PreferencesUpdate.title: PreferencesUpdate
PreferencesUpdate.description:
Body of ``PUT /candidates/me/preferences``: replaces every preference.

Every field is required (an empty list means "no preference") so a client can never wipe
the preferences by omitting a field.

two public roles here also makes the OpenAPI document say so.
